name: radar

provenance.install: the project's own install script, read in full before it was run; radar then orchestrates its own containers
provenance.note: There is a crate named radar on crates.io by a different author, published 2021 and unrelated. `cargo install radar` would have measured it. See AGENTS.md step 1.

run.invocation_evidence: the 2026-09-01 re-run recorded in tools/legacy/normalise_runs.py and its 34 stdout artefacts under raw/radar-c2-2026-09-01/. radar starts its own containers, so the isolation is radar's rather than ours, which is stated rather than claimed otherwise.

layout_reason: radar refuses a target whose Cargo.toml sits at the root of the path it is given, answering `No Cargo.toml files found in any subdirectories` while exiting 0 and writing nothing. Every case is therefore staged as <case>.<variant>/pkg/{Cargo.toml,src} and the wrapper prefix is removed from the locations afterwards. Getting this wrong produces a silent zero that looks exactly like a clean miss.

evidence.means: radar's own count of the files it read, printed whether or not it found anything

output.name: radar.json
output.no_output_reason: radar writes NO output file when it finds nothing. The 2026-08-31 runner decided ok versus unavailable by asking whether the file existed, so a clean zero and a failed run were the same observation, and one clean zero was published as `could not run`. That is error 36, and this flag plus the coverage pattern above is what stops it recurring: the file's absence is a zero only because radar's own stdout says it scanned the files.

measurements.note: 11 / 11 nominal and real, the most quoted figure in this project, and it has NO per-run log. Radar is syntactic so the run is possible; nobody has done it. Named in docs/COVERAGE.md and in the B7 handover.

Re-run per case, per variant, over all 17 built cases on 2026-09-01 against a corpus pinned by digest on both machines first. 34 invocations, 34 ok, zero unavailable, zero stale paths. Superseded c2-radar-complete.json, which was produced before the corpus was rebuilt and had 161 of 238 findings naming files that no longer exist. Both files stay on disk; only this one scores.

Re-measurement of Auditware/radar main at 67348ee (post-#33/#34/#35/#36/#37) against corpus1 at the pinned commit, promised on radar#32 and delivered 2026-09-02. 35 invocations, 35 ok, zero unavailable, deterministic over two passes. Real recall 11/11 unchanged; findings 52 -> 19; firings on already-fixed variants 24 -> 2 (upper bound). Independently confirms the vendor's own reported figures (2 FPs, 11% noise). Run without a docker daemon via the engine shim documented in ENGINEERING-LOG-2026-09-02: vendor engine code unmodified from the checkout at 67348ee, parity-proven against the docker measurement of 206a469 first (52/52 location rows identical, raw/radar-shim-parity-2026-09-02/).
